# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0, LIGHT is yellow, and there are three wires — 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

I hear nothing, so speech is useless to me and I can't receive it. I can only see gestures. This turn I received two gestures:
- From Mute: ✋ ☝ (a hand and a pointing-up finger)
- From Blind: 👋 (a waving hand)

I need to interpret these. But gestures mean nothing until someone establishes meaning — and crucially, Mute and Blind can't see each other's gestures to me (Mute can hear speech; Blind can see gestures). Let me trace the channels:

- Mute → can read the manual, can speak. Mute's speech reaches Blind and Deaf? No — Deaf never receives speech. Mute's speech reaches Blind. Mute's gestures reach Deaf (and Blind, since Blind can see).
- Blind → can touch bomb, can speak. Blind's speech reaches Mute. Blind's gestures reach Deaf (and Mute sees gestures? Mute can see — yes, Mute can see gestures).
- Deaf (me) → speech reaches Mute and Blind. Gestures reach Mute only.

So I can speak to Mute and Blind. I can gesture to Mute only.

The gestures I received don't yet have agreed meanings. I should establish a code. Since I'm first to act in my own turn (I'm Deaf, third in order Mute→Blind→Deaf, so I've already received this round's Mute and Blind messages). Wait — order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Mute and Blind already went this round, and I'm last. Their messages reached me now.

I should reply with speech (to Mute and Blind) and gestures (to Mute). But I need a shared code. The problem: Mute gestured ✋☝ to me, Blind gestured 👋 to me. These are meaningless without agreement.

Best move: propose a simple encoding using speech, since speech reaches both Mute and Blind, and they can both understand words. I'll describe what I see (colors, display, light) in words so both can use it. And I'll propose gesture meanings for future rounds.

Let me describe the bomb clearly:
- DISPLAY: 0
- LIGHT: yellow
- WIRES: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green

I'll speak this to both. I'll also gesture to Mute to confirm I saw their gesture, but gestures need agreed meaning — I'll just acknowledge.

Actually, I should be careful: I can't hear, so I don't know what Mute/Blind said in speech. But they may have spoken too. I only got gestures. So I should just send my observation.

Let me send speech to both (unnamed reaches Mute and Blind), and a gesture to Mute.

For gestures, I'll start establishing: maybe use ✋ to mean "wire" and ☝ to mean "position 1"? But I don't know what Mute meant. Better to keep it simple and just send my info via speech, and use a gesture to acknowledge receipt.

I'll speak the full bomb description. That's the most valuable thing — Blind can't see it, Mute can't see it. Only I can see it. So my job is to relay the visual.

Let me compose:

speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝"])

Wait, gesturing back the same symbols might be confusing. Maybe gesture ✌ (two) to indicate I got two messages? Or just acknowledge. I'll gesture ✋☝ back to show I received Mute's gesture, plus 👋 to show I received Blind's. But Blind can't receive my gestures (only Mute can). Hmm, Blind can see gestures — wait, Blind cannot see. "Blind: Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts. Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind cannot see gestures. Only Mute can see my gestures. And I can only receive gestures from Mute and Blind (they gesture, I see).

So my gesture reaches Mute only. Blind's gesture reached me (I can see). Mute's gesture reached me.

I'll gesture to Mute something meaningful. Let me establish: I'll gesture ✋☝ meaning "I received your hand+point". Actually let me just send a clear acknowledgment and propose a code.

Keep it simple. I'll speak the bomb info to both, and gesture to Mute a confirmation.

Let me finalize.I'm the Deaf monkey. I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0, LIGHT is yellow, and there are three wires — wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.

I hear nothing, so I cannot receive any speech. This turn I received two gestures:
- Mute gestured ✋ ☝ to me
- Blind gestured 👋 to me

These gestures have no agreed meaning yet, so I can't act on them. But I hold the entire visual of the bomb, which neither Mute nor Blind can see. My job is to relay it in words, since my speech reaches both Mute and Blind.

Channel check: my speech reaches Mute and Blind. My gestures reach Mute only (Blind can't see). So I'll speak the bomb description to both, and send a gesture to Mute to acknowledge receipt and start building a shared code.

I'll describe the bomb plainly and propose that ✋ means "wire" going forward, so we can build a gesture vocabulary.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✋]

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✋]

I'm the Deaf monkey. Let me take stock.

The bomb display has stayed at 0 across all three turns. The LIGHT has changed: yellow → blue → white. The wires have stayed constant: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

So the LIGHT is a changing signal — it's not static. That's important. The display is 0, which might be a countdown or a state. The light changing each round suggests it's a live indicator, maybe tied to the bomb's state or a timer.

Now the gestures. I've received a sequence over three turns:
- Turn 1: Mute ✋ ☝ ; Blind 👋
- Turn 2: Mute ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ; Blind ☝ ✋
- Turn 3: Mute ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ; Blind 🤲 ✋

I tried to establish ✋ = "wire" but I never confirmed it with Mute, and gestures have no meaning until agreed. I sent ✋ ☝ back to Mute as acknowledgment. Mute has now sent ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ twice, then ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝. Blind sent 👋, then ☝ ✋, then 🤲 ✋.

I can't decode these reliably. What I *can* do is keep relaying the visual, since that's my unique contribution. The key new fact this turn: LIGHT is now white, and it has changed every round (yellow, blue, white). The display remains 0.

I should tell both Mute and Blind that the light is changing and list the sequence, because that's a pattern only I can see. Blind can't see the light at all; Mute can't see it either. So this is critical information.

I'll speak to both, and gesture to Mute. I still can't confirm gesture meanings, so I'll keep my gesture minimal and consistent — repeat ✋ ☝ to signal I'm receiving, and add a new proposal in words.

Let me report: display 0, light sequence yellow→blue→white, wires unchanged.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: DISPLAY still 0. LIGHT has changed each round: it was yellow, then blue, now white. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The light seems to be a live signal.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: DISPLAY still 0. LIGHT has changed each round: it was yellow, then blue, now white. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The light seems to be a live signal.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲 ✋]

I'm the Deaf monkey. Let me track everything.

The bomb: DISPLAY stays at 0 every round. LIGHT has cycled yellow → blue → white → red. Wires constant: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

So the LIGHT is cycling through colors each turn. That's a strong pattern — it's a moving indicator, not a fixed state. The display never moves off 0.

Gestures received:
- Turn 1: Mute ✋ ☝ ; Blind 👋
- Turn 2: Mute ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ; Blind ☝ ✋
- Turn 3: Mute ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ; Blind 🤲 ✋
- Turn 4: Mute ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ; Blind 🤲 ✋

Mute alternates between ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ and ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ (first symbol changes: ✋ then ✊ then ✋). Blind has settled into 🤲 ✋ for the last two turns.

I still have no agreed gesture code, so I can't decode these. I sent ✋ ☝ to Mute twice as acknowledgment but never got confirmation of meaning. My real value is the visual relay.

New fact this turn: LIGHT is now red. The sequence so far: yellow, blue, white, red. That's four distinct colors, one per turn. This looks like a repeating cycle or a sequence I should keep reporting.

I'll keep relaying to both Mute and Blind via speech, and gesture to Mute. I should also try harder to establish a code — maybe explicitly propose in words that I'll gesture the light color, so Mute can map it. But Mute can't see the light; only I can. So if I gesture a color code, Mute learns the light color from me. That's useful — but we need agreed symbols for colors, and there are no color gestures in the alphabet. So I can only describe colors in words (speech), which reaches both.

So speech is my channel for colors. Good. I'll keep doing that.

Let me report the light sequence and note the cycle.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: DISPLAY still 0. LIGHT sequence so far: yellow, blue, white, now red. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The light cycles one color per round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: DISPLAY still 0. LIGHT sequence so far: yellow, blue, white, now red. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. The light cycles one color per round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝"])
```
